en: Yesterday: a clock tower strikes six times, in five seconds. How long for twelve strikes?
The answer is eleven seconds. Not ten!
Six strikes have only five gaps between them.
Five gaps, in five seconds. So each gap is one second.
Twelve strikes have eleven gaps. So, eleven seconds.
Person one stands at a well, with two empty jugs.
One jug holds exactly three litres. The other holds exactly five litres.
There are no markings on the jugs, and there is plenty of water.
Person one needs exactly four litres of water.
No guessing. No filling halfway. So how does Person one do it?
